# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

# Repository Exploration Report: Transaction Enrichment Service

## 1. Overall Repo Structure

`/app` contains a single Python Flask microservice (the Dockerfile copies it as `transaction-enrichment-python`) that enriches Indian bank statement rows with categories, sub-categories, merchant types, and payee names.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                      # python:3.9.2, gunicorn on port 9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                    # Flask 1.1.2, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, scipy, sklearn
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py             # Flask app factory + request timing (lines 7-28)
        ├── Controller.py           # HTTP endpoints, per-bank dispatch (936 lines)
        ├── BankScripts/            # 35 per-bank rule modules (HDFC, SBI, ICICI, Axis, Kotak, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/         # shared enrichment logic + regex constants
```

Pipeline (per request to `POST /categorizeTransaction`, `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py:69`): bank-specific categorizer → `card_clean_names`/`card_purpose` (credit cards) → `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` (SAVING only) → optional `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()`. There is also `POST /recurrentTransactions` (`Controller.py:55`).

## 2. Key Files and Functions

### Categorization (transactionCategory)
Each bank script builds a `conditions_choices` list of regex conditions evaluated with `np.select`, default `"TRANSFER"`. Representative example:
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py:9` — `categorize_HDFC_transactions(transactions, accountType)`; category rules at lines 11–104, subcategory rules 112–132, partyName extraction 146–273.
- Same shape in all 35 `BankScripts/*.py` (e.g. `IDFC.py:8`, `Central.py:8`, `Kotak.py`, `SBI.py`, ...).
- Cross-bank second pass: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:9` — `purpose(transactions, accountType)` assigns `transactionSubcategory` (lines 12–152), overrides `transactionCategory` (154–170), and assigns `merchantType` (182–278) using shared regex constants.
- Shared keyword dictionaries: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` (SALARY line 6, LOAN/LOAN_REP lines 9–14, CREDIT_CARD line 20, etc.) and `BankRegexConstants.py` (per-bank patterns).
- Category/subcategory display enums: `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py:3`, `UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py:3`.

### Payee / counterparty extraction (partyName)
- Split helpers: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py:14-45` — `sep_by_` (slash), `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_wave`, `sep_by_star`, `sep_by_colon`, etc.; regex extractor `py_extract` at `AppUtil.py:61`; `fuzzy_match` at line 48.
- Per-bank extraction blocks, e.g. `HDFC.py:146-273` (UPI/IMPS/NEFT dash-position rules, POS pattern `HDFC_POS_PATTERN` at `BankRegexConstants.py:76`), `IDFC.py:68-103`, `Central.py:63-92`.
- Post-hoc cleanup: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py:9` — `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` (1971 lines of bank-specific normalization); CC variant `CardCleanNames.py:9` — `card_clean_names`.

### Cheque detection
- Category rules per bank, e.g. `HDFC.py:69-75` (CHEQUE_RETURN / CHEQUE_PAID / CHEQUE_DEPOSIT via `\bCHQ\b`, `CHQ DEP RET`, etc.) and `HDFC.py:100` (15-char remark `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT); `Central.py:45-46`; `IDFC.py:27,42-43`.
- Cheque payee patterns: `BankRegexConstants.py:81-90` (`HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1`–`10`, MICR clearing formats), applied in `HDFC.py:188-197`; PNB cheque patterns `BankRegexConstants.py:140-148`; UCO at 380-383; Kotak `CHQ_PATTERN1-4` at 314-317 with bank-name stripper `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` at line 318.

### Transfer direction keywords (to/from)
- `BankRegexConstants.py:241-298` — `FT_PATTERN0-19` ("FUNDS TRF TO", "FUND TRANSFER FROM/FRM", "TRF FROM") and `FT_CHQ_PATTERN1-37` (dozens of "TRF/TRNS/FTR ... TO/FROM" variants); IB direction patterns `IB_PATTERN2/3/5/6` at 303-307; Kotak "Received from"/"Sent to" (`RCVD_FROM_IMPS1-5` at 234-238, `MB_TFR1` at 188, `STOP_STRINGS` at 191) used in `Kotak.py:243-254`; HDFC FT patterns `HDFC_FT_PATTERN1-7` at 93-99 applied in `HDFC.py:200-213`; "Sent to:/Received from" also in `Paytm.py:75-83` and `AuSmallFinanceBank.py:54-83`; HDFC clean-up of "Trf To/Paid To/Fund Trf To" at `HDFC.py:255-257`.

### Slash-delimited references (BILLPAY-type with 4 fields)
- `IDFC.py:30` — `BILLPAY/` → `BILL_PAYMENT` category.
- `Central.py:64-65` — 4-field slash refs: `/BILLPAYMENT/|/Tech Process/` → `sep_by_(description,3,4)` (take 4th slash field); 3-field variant takes field index 2–3.
- Generic slash-count-based extraction throughout: `Indusind.py:193-210` (`count("/").eq(5..10)`), `Federal.py:75-90`, `ICICI.py:147-165` (`^BIL/INFT/`, `^INF/INFT/`), `UnionBank.py:91-103`, `PNB.py:97-137`, `IDBI.py:96`, `SouthIndian.py:70-72`, `HDFC.py:201`.
- Kotak "BILLPAY FOR" (colon/space-delimited): `BankRegexConstants.py:171-175` (`BILL_PAY_KOTAK1-5`), category at `Kotak.py:47`.

### Salary sub-tagging
- Keyword pass: `Purpose.py:14-17` using `SALARY` (`RegexConstants.py:6`), `NOT_SAL` (line 7), `SAL_IMPS` (line 190), `SALARY_DISB` (line 88, → SALARY_DISBURSED for CURRENT accounts).
- Bank-specific: `HDFC.py:119,124-125` (e.g. `^A2AINT01` → SALARY; 6-digit-only credit narration on SAVINGS → SALARY); salary stop-word stripping in partyName at `HDFC.py:141-142, 217, 234-235`.
- Statistical detector: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py:16` — `salary_detection(transactions)`: Levenshtein-distance clustering of partyName into `Group_ID` (lines 23-34), candidate filtering (42-53), mode-amount / frequency heuristics (64-110), propagation by group (116-122), REIMBURSEMENT reassignment (<30% of max salary, lines 125-140, 196-202), and second-salary detection (142-194). Invoked only for `accountType == "SAVING"` from Controller.
- Pension → SALARY: `Purpose.py:286`.

### Reversal / bounce detection
- Reversals per bank, e.g. `HDFC.py:21-25` (CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL, UPI_REVERSAL `REV-UPI|UPI RET-`, IMPS_REVERSAL, ATM_REVERSAL, generic REVERSAL) and heuristic paired-row reversal at `HDFC.py:98` (CREDIT following DEBIT of same amount/description); `IDFC.py:15-19`; shared constants `REVERSAL_CANARA` (`BankRegexConstants.py:323`), `REVERSAL_KV` (344), `REVERSAL_CITY` (349), `REVERSAL_UCO` (376), `REVERSAL_YES` (394), `REVERSAL_RBL` (412), `REVERSAL_FEDERAL` (401).
- Bounces: AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE at `HDFC.py:27` and paired-row rule `HDFC.py:99`; ECS penalties `HDFC.py:26`, `ECS_PENAL*` constants (`BankRegexConstants.py:111, 340, 369, 387, 411`); cheque-bounce reason classification in `Purpose.py:145-147` using `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` (`RegexConstants.py:86`) and `INSUFF_BOUNCE` (line 87) → TECHNICAL_BOUNCE / INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE; balance-based bounce `HDFC.py:126` (CHEQUE_PAID followed by CHEQUE_RETURN with negative balance → INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE).

### Other enrichment
- Internal transfers: `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py:8` — `internal_payment()` fuzzy-matches partyName against account holder (75% ratio) and sets `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` / `isInternalPayment`.
- PFM: `PFMCategorization.py:8` — `pfm_categorization`; `SimpleDescription.py:6` — `simple_description`.
- Recurrence: `RecurrentTxns.py:8` — `recurrent_transactions`.

## 3. How Tests Are Run

There is no test suite. Findings:
- No `test_*.py`/`*_test*` files, no `tests/` directory, no pytest/tox/CI configuration anywhere in the repo (only `.gitignore`, `Dockerfile`, `setup.py`).
- `setup.py` declares no test dependencies; the only "testing" artifact is commented-out dendrogram plotting inside `SalaryDetection.py:27-32`.
- Validation appears to be manual/integration-style: build and run the service (`docker build` then gunicorn serves `categorizationapp:app` on port 9898, or `pip3 install -e . && python -m categorizationapp`) and exercise `POST /categorizeTransaction` (payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, optional `isPFMEnabled`, and a `transactions` array with `description`, `amount`, `type`, `remark`, `balanceAfterTransaction`, `transactionDate`) or `POST /recurrentTransactions`.

steps.message:
All five faults found and fixed — each was a single-token boundary/offset flip inside an otherwise-correct rule, exactly as the maintainer predicted.

## Fixes

**1. All-numeric remark credit → generic transfer instead of cheque deposit** (mango_saver A)
`BankScripts/HDFC.py:100` — the rule required `remark.str.len().eq(15)` while its own regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 chars, so it could never fire. HDFC's sibling remark rules (HDFC.py:214-215: `^N[0-9]{15}$`, `^[0-9]{16}$`) confirm the field is 16 chars wide. Fixed `eq(15)` → `eq(16)`.

**2. Bare numeric narration credit lost SALARY sub-tag** (mango_saver B)
`BankScripts/HDFC.py:124` — checked `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the Controller and every other bank script pass `"SAVING"`, so the condition was always false. Fixed to `"SAVING"`.

**3. Leading direction-word narration → empty/wrong counterparty** (rk_ontheroad)
`BankScripts/ICICI.py:159` — `py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 0 (the word "TO"/"FROM") instead of group 1 (the name); "To" was then wiped to empty by a later cleanup, "From" survived as a wrong name. Fixed `index=0` → `index=1`.

**4. Four-field slash bill ref lifts numeric reference as payee** (auditlens)
`BankScripts/ICICI.py:147` — for `BIL/INFT/<numeric-ref>/<payee>` (exactly 3 slashes) it took slash field 2 (`sep_by_(...,2,3)` = the numeric ref) instead of the final field. Since `BIL/INFT` is categorized INTERNAL_FUND_TRANSFER, the numeric-name scrubber deliberately skips it, so the number leaked through. Fixed to `sep_by_(...,3,4)`.

**5. Offsetting credit right after its debit recorded as bounce, not reversal** (maintainer)
`BankScripts/HDFC.py:98` — the paired-row reversal rule compared `description` against `shift(periods=2)` while type/amount used `periods=1` (the ICICI sibling at ICICI.py:49 uses 1 throughout), so it never matched and rows fell through to the next rule's AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE. Fixed to `periods=1`.

## Verification
Ran synthetic rows for each complaint through the actual categorizers (and full `categorize → purpose → clean_names` pipeline):
- 16-digit zero-padded remark credit → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`
- `123456` credit on SAVING → subcategory `SALARY`
- `TRFR FROM:RAMESH KUMAR` → `Ramesh Kumar`; `TRFR TO:SURESH GUPTA` → `Suresh Gupta`
- `BIL/INFT/003327628067/AJAY SHARMA` → `Ajay Sharma`
- identical debit→credit pair → `REVERSAL`, while a non-transfer identical pair still correctly yields `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`

A batch of ordinary rows (UPI/POS/NEFT/IMPS/ATM/cheque/interest for both banks) still enriches exactly as before, so no currently-correct rows shift.
